subject: Re: Post-call: model fit benchmarks & next steps
messages:
From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up from today's call — model fit info

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call today — that was super helpful. As we discussed, the priority for Acme is a model that balances throughput for our real-time recommendation endpoint (target p50 latency < 120ms at 200 TPS) while preserving quality for short multi-turn prompts (customer intent + context).

Could you share:
- Redwood-recommended model variants for this workload
- Any benchmark links, prompt sets, or example evals you can run against our seed prompts
- Typical latency/TPS profiles you see for those models (p50/p95 at reference batch sizes)

We have a short prompt set (about 150 examples) I'll share after NDA — want to understand if Redwood sees any quality regressions compared to our current production model.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Liu
Sr. Product Manager, Recommendations
Acme Retail
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — model fit info

Hi Samantha — great talking earlier. A quick recap and the artifacts you asked for below.

Recommended model variants (based on your target latency and context lengths):
- redwood-realtime-7b: lowest-latency variant, good for strict p50 SLAs 
  - Typical perf (reference: 1x A100-like GPU, seq len 128, batching tuned): TPS ~ 220, p50 ~ 95ms, p95 ~ 310ms
- redwood-balanced-13b: higher quality, still optimizable for throughput
  - Typical perf: TPS ~ 85, p50 ~ 160ms, p95 ~ 420ms
- redwood-13b-quant-q4: quantized option for cost-sensitive production with ~10-15% quality delta on some instruction-style prompts
  - Typical perf: TPS ~ 140, p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 340ms

I've uploaded a short benchmark summary and the seed prompt set we typically use for recommendation-style evals. Links/attachments below. Note that these numbers are Redwood-verified performance profiles measured against our internal model catalog with continuous batching and KV caching enabled — your real results will depend on sequence length distribution and routing policy.

Attachments included: acme_benchmark_summary_20260322.xlsx (overview of throughput + latency percentiles for the above variants).

Useful links:
- Benchmark dashboard (redwood-verified): https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/acme-2026-model-fit
- Prompt sets and example evals: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cBenchmarkPromptSets
- HubSpot deal: https://crm.redwood.example.com/deals/ACME-2026-042

Quality/regression notes: we run model-level regression checks tied to prompt sets — if you share your 150 examples we can run a pre-deployment evaluation and surface metrics (exact-match, BLEU-ish similarity, and a calibrated human-score proxy). For production, we recommend a canary rollout where we monitor the quality signal and have an automatic rollback if an overall quality delta > 3% on the monitored prompt set is observed.

Next steps I propose:
1) You share the 150 seed prompts (drive link or attached doc)
2) We run an initial eval against redwood-realtime-7b and redwood-balanced-13b and return a short report (2-3 business days)
3) If perf and quality look good, pilot with a small percentage of traffic and enable regression alerts and auto-fallback to the current model variant

I'll loop Alex in as the engineering contact — he'll help with any test harness or tokenization details.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acmeretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
Cc: Acme Retail IT <it@acmeretail.com>
Date: 2026-03-21T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — model fit info

Hi Marissa — this is great, thanks. A few quick clarifying Qs before we hand over the prompt set:

1) For the redwood-realtime-7b numbers, are those with batching enabled (what batch size)? We expect a lot of small, low-latency requests from web clients.
2) How do you measure the "human-score proxy" you mentioned? Is that something we can customize?
3) On regression alerts: can we set per-route thresholds? We want stricter quality monitoring for purchase-intent prompts vs. generic browsing prompts.

I'll attach the seed prompt file in a follow-up once we confirm measurement details and the NDA.

— Samantha
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example.com>
To: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.example.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.example.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today's call — model fit info

Thanks — answers inline and next steps:

1) redwood-realtime-7b numbers: yes, those are with continuous batching enabled and a target micro-batch size of ~8 for small requests. For strictly single-request, low-latency paths we can tune to micro-batch=1 and you can expect p50 to increase ~15-30ms depending on network hops. We'll capture both profiles in the report we run against your prompts.

2) Human-score proxy: we use a small calibrated classifier that maps automated signals (semantic-similarity, length-normalized token overlap, and a small set of learned heuristics) to a 0-100 score that correlates with blind human ratings on our internal evals. Yes — it's customizable. We can weight false positives/negatives differently for the purchase-intent set and run a custom rubric you provide.

3) Per-route thresholds: absolutely — Redwood lets you configure route-level alerts and different fallback policies. Typical configuration:
- Purchase-intent route: stricter alert threshold (quality delta > 1.5%) and automatic fallback to redwood-balanced-13b for 5 minutes then re-evaluate
- Browse/assist route: more permissive (quality delta > 3%) and gradual throttling

I've attached a short mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_acme_20260322.pdf) that outlines the pilot scope, responsibilities, and proposed timeline.

Next practical steps:
- If you can send the 150 prompts, we'll kickoff the eval and deliver the benchmark report within 48-72 hours.
- Alex (cc'd) can provision a sandbox endpoint and share a short test harness (tokenization + client example) so you can run a smoke test locally.

Would Thursday 10am PT work for a quick 20-min sync to review results?

Cheers,
Marissa
